task.title: Relics: teach agents to use relics and store the design as the first relic
task.description:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

This story finishes the first working version. It documents relics, teaches agents to use them, and then stores the relic design itself as the first relic so the remaining stories can point at it.

## Documentation

- `README.md`, `docs/reference.md` and `docs/architecture.md` gain relic sections, with a small object-graph example of a relic ref.
- The reference currently says a long document "belongs in the repository with the task linking to it". That sentence changes to point at relics.
- Everything documented exists. Commands from later stories are left out or clearly marked as not yet built.

## Agent guidelines and skill

The generated guidelines (`workbook docs update`) and the Workbook skill explain:

- how to find the relics linked to a task and read one part;
- how to edit a part safely, naming the version it was read at;
- that two edits to the same body are reported as a conflict;
- that on a conflict the agent reads the current version and saves again when the intent is clear, and otherwise shows the user both versions and asks;
- that a relic ID looks like `WB-R-…` and a task ID like `WB-…`.

## Store the design as the first relic

- Create a relic of type `spec` from the approved design, with one part per section and one part per decision, so that stories can link to the exact part they build. Use the part types the default schemas will later make official: `section`, `decision` and `open-question`.
- Link each remaining relic story's task from the part it builds, with the relationship `implemented-by`.
- Confirm the relic is shared through `origin` and readable from a fresh clone.
- Remove the untracked `specs/2026-11-21-relics-design.html` copy once the relic is confirmed, and update the note at the end of each remaining story's description to point at the relic.

## Done when

- A fresh clone can read the design relic and follow a link from any remaining relic story to the part it builds.
- The documentation matches the commands that exist.
- An agent given only the generated guidelines can find, read and safely edit a relic.

## Not in this story

Schemas, relic-to-relic links, history and diff commands, and the web page.

## Where the design is

The approved design is "Workbook Relics Design" (2026-11-21). It is kept out of the repository. Until "Relics: teach agents to use relics and store the design as the first relic" is done, an untracked copy sits at `specs/2026-11-21-relics-design.html` in Dylan's checkout. After that, read the relic. This description carries what the story needs, and the design wins where the two disagree.
